To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The network of coupled chaotic logistic maps exhibits a phase transition from an ordered state with a single giant component to a disordered state with many components as the rewiring probability increases; 2) The transition is sharp and the critical rewiring probability is independent of the number of units in the network; 3) In the disordered state, the network is scale-free with a power-law distribution of degree; 4) The degree distribution in the ordered state is not scale-free;
the network formed by chaotic logistic maps has a power-law degree distribution and that the network is divided into communities, which are not static but change over time.
